name: Trabuco Burch–sling trial
aliases: Burch versus midurethral sling at sacrocolpopexy
question: At open abdominal sacrocolpopexy in women with stress or occult stress incontinence, does a retropubic midurethral sling improve continence compared with Burch urethropexy?

design.blinding: patients and stress-test assessors masked, although suprapubic sling incisions could reveal allocation

arms.label: Abdominal sacrocolpopexy with retropubic midurethral sling
abdominal sacrocolpopexy with Burch retropubic urethropexy

design.population: Women aged at least 21 years with symptomatic stage II or greater apical or anterior prolapse and symptomatic stress, stress-predominant mixed, or occult stress incontinence who chose open abdominal sacrocolpopexy at two US centers.
design.locator: 2016 full text, Materials and Methods and Results; Table 1

verdictNote: Neither six-month coprimary continence endpoint met the prespecified P < 0.05 threshold.
takeaway: At open abdominal sacrocolpopexy, retropubic midurethral sling and Burch urethropexy did not differ significantly in overall or stress-specific continence at six months; sling recipients reported greater satisfaction.

reports.label: Six-month randomized report
reports.citation: Trabuco EC, Klingele CJ, Blandon RE, et al. "Burch Retropubic Urethropexy Compared With Midurethral Sling With Concurrent Sacrocolpopexy: A Randomized Controlled Trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2016;128(4):828-835. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000001651
reports.followUp: 6 months after surgery; 53/57 sling and 51/56 Burch participants assessed

results.measure: Six-month composite of negative stress test, no SUI retreatment, and ICIQ-SF score 0; intention-to-treat
results.note: Odds ratio compares sling with Burch; two-sided prespecified P < 0.05 threshold. The sample plan had 80% power for a 25-point difference assuming 63% Burch continence.

results.measure: Six-month negative stress test, no SUI retreatment, and no self-reported stress leakage; intention-to-treat
results.note: Odds ratio compares sling with Burch; two-sided prespecified P < 0.05 threshold.

results.measure: Satisfied at six months among respondents
results.note: Respondent denominators differ from randomized arm sizes.

results.measure: Urgency incontinence resolved by six months among those affected at baseline

delivery.note: All fellowship-trained surgeons had performed more than 20 procedures of each incontinence type before enrollment.
